metadata.summary: BraTS 2024 is a multi-institutional, international challenge dataset providing multi-parametric MRI scans and ground truth annotations for brain tumor segmentation, survival prediction, and molecular marker classification. It includes sub-challenges for post-treatment glioma (~2,200 patients), pre-treatment glioma (~1,250 training cases plus additional), pediatric tumors (~2,490), meningioma (~650), brain metastases (~460), and an Africa subset (~750). An unseen test set contains over 4,000 patients. A histopathology extension with 280,000 tiles is also included.
metadata.purpose: To advance AI methods for brain tumor segmentation, survival prediction, and molecular marker classification via a standardized benchmark.
metadata.avoided_uses: Commercial deployment without further validation; clinical decision-making without regulatory approval.
creators: MICCAI Brain Tumor Segmentation Challenge Organizers

papers.title: BraTS 2024: Diverse tasks for brain tumor segmentation, survival prediction, and molecular marker classification

modality.scope: Brain tumors (glioma, meningioma, metastases, pediatric tumors)

ethics.privacy_measures: All data de-identified prior to release; no protected health information included.
ethics.legal_compliance: Complies with Synapse platform terms and challenge-specific data use restrictions.

known_limitations: Lack of granular demographic reporting (age, sex, ethnicity) limits subgroup fairness analysis.
Convenience sampling from volunteer clinical sites may introduce selection bias.
Uneven distribution across tumor types and regions (e.g., Africa subset ~750 vs. pediatric ~2,490) affects statistical power for some subgroups.
Histopathology extension (280k tiles) lacks patient-level linkage to MRI data in source text.
Test set is unseen and unannotated — performance on it cannot be validated without challenge submission.
bias_and_limitations.modifications: Data are de-identified and standardized to NIfTI format; no synthetic data generation reported.
bias_and_limitations.representativeness_concerns: Overrepresentation of high-resource academic centers; underrepresentation of low- and middle-income country (LMIC) sites outside the dedicated Africa subset.
bias_and_limitations.long_tail_classes: Meningioma (~650) and brain metastases (~460) are substantially smaller than pediatric (~2,490) and glioma (~3,450) subsets.
bias_and_limitations.generalizability_statement: Designed for cross-institutional and cross-population generalizability, but limited by lack of demographic metadata and uneven geographic/tumor-type sampling.
bias_and_limitations.subgroup_coverage: Coverage includes pediatric, African, and multiple tumor-type subgroups; however, age, sex, and ethnicity distributions are not reported.
bias_and_limitations.missing_data: Demographic metadata (age, sex, ethnicity) is not provided in source text.

tasks_and_use.excluded_tasks: Real-time clinical inference; direct diagnostic use without regulatory clearance.

data_origin.selection_rationale: Cases selected to represent diverse brain tumor types (glioma, pediatric tumors, meningioma, metastases) and geographic/clinical settings (including Africa subset), enabling evaluation of generalizability across subpopulations and disease states.
data_origin.sampling_strategy: Multi-site, convenience sampling from participating clinical centers; stratified by tumor type and treatment status.
data_origin.aggregation_multisource: Aggregated from multiple international clinical sites; no explicit harmonization method described in source text.

population.target_population: Patients with brain tumors including glioma (pre- and post-treatment), pediatric brain tumors, meningioma, brain metastases, and cases from African institutions.
population.inclusion_criteria: Diagnosis of relevant brain tumor type; availability of mpMRI and corresponding annotations.
population.missing_groups: No explicit reporting on underrepresented groups beyond the inclusion of an Africa subset; absence of detailed demographic reporting implies potential underrepresentation of non-African, non-pediatric, non-glioma populations in certain sub-challenges.
population.subgroups_disparate_outcomes: Pediatric, African, and metastatic subgroups may face differential outcomes due to disparities in access, imaging protocols, or annotation consistency — not explicitly assessed but flagged as high-risk for bias.

annotation.annotation_method: Expert radiologist/pathologist annotation; histopathology tiles annotated by pathologists.
annotation.labeling_provenance: Ground truth annotations provided by expert readers per challenge protocol; histopathology extension includes 280,000 expert-annotated tiles.
